It has been going on steadily for about ten months now, starting shortly after my mother's health issues began, so it's definitely been longer than three months.\n\nDoctor: When these episodes happen, do you feel a strong sense that you cannot stop eating or control how much you eat, and do they leave you feeling upset, guilty, or distressed afterward?\n\nPatient: Yes, once I start, it really feels like a switch flips and I'm powerless to stop, even though a part of my brain is screaming at me to put the food down. Afterward, I feel deeply ashamed, worn out, and sluggish, which leaves me dragging through work the next day and wanting to avoid social plans altogether.\n\nDoctor: Do you find that your self-worth is strongly tied to your weight or body shape, or that you feel driven to diet because of fear of gaining weight?\n\nPatient: I haven't really been focusing on my weight, body shape, or dieting. My main concern right now is just dealing with the stress, feeling so out of control with food, and the exhaustion and shame that follow.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever intentionally restrict food, diet because you’re afraid of gaining weight, or feel that your self-worth is strongly tied to your body shape or weight?\n\nPatient: No, I don't restrict my food or diet because of weight fears, and my self-worth isn't really tied to my body shape or weight. My main struggle is truly just the out-of-control eating episodes and managing the massive stress of my daily life. Dieting and body image aren't really what is driving this.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had times when you eat very little or avoid food on purpose, or do your eating episodes happen without any regular dieting or food restriction?\n\nPatient: I don't intentionally restrict my food or try to diet. However, because of my hectic schedule juggling work and my mom's care, I often end up postponing meals until late in the evening. It's really just a lack of time during the day rather than a deliberate choice to skip eating.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period where you intentionally tried to lose weight or felt very preoccupied with your body shape or weight, even if that was not the main problem now?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really focused on dieting or trying to lose weight in the past. My main concern has always been the stress and these out-of-control eating episodes themselves, rather than my body shape or weight.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period where you intentionally tried to lose weight, felt very preoccupied with your body shape or weight, or did anything to undo eating such as vomiting, laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise?\n\nPatient: No, I've never done any of those things to try and undo my eating. I also haven't been focused on trying to lose weight or dieting lately.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period where you felt strongly preoccupied with your weight or body shape, or felt driven to diet or lose weight because of how you looked?\n\nPatient: No, I've never really been preoccupied with my weight or body shape, and I haven't felt a strong drive to diet. My focus and stress have always been completely centered on my work, caring for my mom, and trying to handle this out-of-control eating pattern itself.\n\nDoctor: During these episodes, do you usually eat much more than most people would in a similar amount of time, with a clearly large amount of food rather than just snacking or grazing?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is definitely a large amount of food, far more than just grazing. On a typical night, I'll plow through a full takeout dinner, half a loaf of buttered bread, a big bowl of cereal, and various pantry snacks in one sitting. It is way more than my daughter or coworkers would ever eat, but I just keep going until it's all gone.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt that your self-worth depends on your weight or body shape, or found yourself dieting mainly because you were afraid of gaining weight?\n\nPatient: No, I've never really felt that way or focused on my weight. My struggle is completely about the out-of-control eating when I'm stressed and exhausted, rather than any dieting or body image issues.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever worry a lot about your weight or body shape, or intentionally diet or restrict food because you’re afraid of gaining weight?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really worry about my weight or body shape, nor do I intentionally diet or restrict food out of fear of gaining weight. Postponing my meals during the day is just a result of my busy schedule and being on the run, rather than an attempt to restrict.\n\nDoctor: Just to confirm, have you ever had any episodes of self-induced vomiting, laxative use, fasting, or excessive exercise to try to prevent weight gain after eating, even once in the past?\n\nPatient: No, I have never done any of those things, not even once. I've never made myself throw up, used laxatives, fasted, or exercised excessively to try to compensate for the eating.\n\nDoctor: Before these evening eating episodes, do you usually go long periods without eating or intentionally skip meals, or do the binges happen even when you’ve been eating regularly during the day?\n\nPatient: With my hectic schedule commuting between work and my mom's care, I do often postpone meals or just grab something quick on the run. However, these late-night episodes happen even when I'm not actually hungry, sometimes even when I'm still full from a late afternoon snack. It's usually triggered the moment I sit down with my planner and start worrying about all my responsibilities.\n\nDoctor: Just to make sure I understand, have you ever had any concerns about your weight or body shape, or ever tried to compensate for these eating episodes by dieting, fasting, vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise?\n\nPatient: No, I have never used any of those methods like vomiting, fasting, laxatives, or excessive exercise to compensate for the eating. I don't really have concerns about my weight or body shape, as my main focus has just been on the out-of-control eating itself.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 3 months where you regularly had binge-eating episodes but also felt very preoccupied with your weight or body shape, or tried to prevent weight gain by dieting, fasting, vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise?\n\nPatient: Yes, I have been having these regular episodes four or five nights a week for about ten months now. However, I have never tried to prevent weight gain by throwing up, fasting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively. While I feel deeply ashamed of the eating itself, I've just never engaged in those types of compensatory behaviors.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a time when your eating episodes were mainly driven by fear of gaining weight or a strong focus on your body shape, even if you did not actually purge or diet?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced that at all. My eating episodes are driven by stress and worry about my mom and work, rather than any fear of gaining weight or concerns about my body shape.\n\nDoctor: When these eating episodes happen, do they usually start because of stress, sadness, anxiety, or feeling overwhelmed, rather than because of hunger or cravings for specific foods?\n\nPatient: Yes, absolutely, they are triggered entirely by stress and anxiety rather than actual physical hunger. As soon as I sit down at the kitchen table with my planner and start worrying about work deadlines and my mom’s medical appointments, I find myself going back and forth to the fridge on autopilot. I'll do this even if I'm already feeling completely full from grabbing a bite to eat earlier in the evening.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period when you were intentionally trying to lose weight or felt very preoccupied with your body shape, even if you did not purge or exercise excessively?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really focused on dieting or been preoccupied with my body shape. My main struggle has just been managing the overwhelming stress and these out-of-control eating episodes themselves.\n\nDoctor: Do these eating episodes happen mainly when you feel stressed, anxious, sad, or overwhelmed, rather than because you are worried about your weight or body shape?\n\nPatient: Yes, they are completely driven by stress and feeling overwhelmed by my daily responsibilities, like managing my mom's care and work deadlines, rather than any concern about my weight. When I sit down at night with my planner, the worry triggers this autopilot eating, which feels like a way to numb out from all the pressure.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any periods where you were intentionally trying to lose weight, felt strongly preoccupied with your body shape or weight, or used behaviors like fasting, vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain?\n\nPatient: No, I've never tried any of those extreme behaviors like vomiting, laxatives, or fasting. I also haven't been intentionally trying to lose weight or focused on my body shape, as my main struggle has truly just been these late-night eating episodes.\n\nDoctor: Have these binge-eating episodes also happened during periods when you felt depressed or lost interest in things, or do they mainly happen only when you are stressed or overwhelmed?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I've felt depressed or lost interest in things; these episodes definitely happen when I am stressed, worried, and overwhelmed by my caregiving duties and work. I only stopped doing my usual activities, like my yoga classes and trail walks, because I simply ran out of time and energy to do them.\n\nDoctor: During the times when the eating happens, have you also been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or losing interest/pleasure in things most days for at least two weeks?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really feel persistently sad or hopeless. Instead, I just feel incredibly stressed, overwhelmed, and exhausted by trying to manage my mom's care alongside my job, and I carry a lot of shame about these eating habits.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever wake up from sleep to eat, or do these episodes only happen while you are fully awake in the evening?\n\nPatient: No, I never wake up from sleep to eat; these episodes always happen in the evening while I'm fully awake, usually while I'm planning the next day or waiting for my daughter and mom to settle down. In fact, I actually end up staying up quite late just trying to digest all the food before I can even go to sleep.\n\nDoctor: Do these eating episodes ever happen while you are half asleep or after waking up during the night, or do they only happen when you are fully awake and aware in the evening?\n\nPatient: I am completely awake and conscious when this happens, never while asleep or after waking up in the middle of the night. I’m usually wide awake at the kitchen table checking emails, working on my planner, or waiting for my daughter and mom to go to bed before I start. Even though it feels like I'm on autopilot and powerless to stop, I am fully aware of what I'm doing.\n\nDoctor: How old were you when these eating episodes first started, and did they begin before or after age 25?\n\nPatient: I am currently 54 years old, and these episodes only started about ten months ago when I was 53. So, they definitely began well after the age of 25.\n\nDoctor: Did these binge-eating episodes first begin before age 25, or did they start later in adulthood?\n\nPatient: They started much later in adulthood, specifically about ten months ago when my mother's health issues began. I never experienced anything like this when I was younger, so it definitely wasn't something I struggled with before age 25.\n\nDoctor: Did these eating episodes begin only after your mother's health problems started, or had you ever had similar episodes earlier in life before this recent stress?\n\nPatient: Yes, they only started about ten months ago, right after my mother's health issues began and my stress levels went into overdrive. I never experienced any kind of out-of-control eating episodes earlier in my life before this recent stressful period."
